PullRequest.Title: Use TextMate highlighting in component fixtures
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- load VS Code's shipped TextMate grammars and Oniguruma WASM for component fixtures
- register fixture languages and synchronously tokenize fixture text models after the async runtime setup
- use the Dark 2026 TextMate palette for Dark fixtures and monochrome token text for non-Dark themes
- reference-count the shared tokenizer installation and safely restore an existing token palette

The shared fixture Dark color theme remains Dark Modern in this PR. Switching the fixture default to Dark 2026 stays separate, and fully scoped multi-theme token palettes remain tracked by #335530.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm exec eslint -- src\vs\workbench\test\browser\componentFixtures\fixtureResourceLoader.ts src\vs\workbench\test\browser\componentFixtures\fixtureSyntaxHighlighting.ts src\vs\workbench\test\browser\componentFixtures\fixtureSyntaxHighlighting.test.ts src\vs\workbench\test\browser\componentFixtures\fixtureUtils.ts`
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\test\browser\componentFixtures\fixtureSyntaxHighlighting.test.ts` (6 passing)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The unconditional critical-path call, resource loader, grammar construction, and teardown are directly traced. HTTP caching may reduce later physical I/O, but parsing/construction and the await remain; only exact duration is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: XHR/filesystem grammar reads, grammar parsing, and tokenizer construction CPU
Findings.PerformanceScaling: In serial screenshot/CI rendering, fixture-scoped disposal drops the final shared reference after each fixture, so grammar setup repeats with fixture/theme count; non-editor fixtures also pay the cost.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Blocked fixture startup and reduced screenshot/CI throughput
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Fixtures awaited their requested UI/file-icon theme before options.render; non-editor fixtures did not initialize Oniguruma or TextMate grammars.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every fixture now awaits TextMate setup before its render callback. Acquisition creates the Oniguruma runtime, a TMGrammarFactory, and tokenizers for seven root languages; final-reference disposal clears the shared instance.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 1164 unconditionally awaits registerFixtureSyntaxHighlighting on every component fixture's render critical path.
Findings.Title: Initialize TextMate only for fixtures that render text models
Findings.Impact: Rendering even simple Buttons or Toggles fixtures now waits for grammar resource loading/parsing. Serial fixture capture can reconstruct grammars for each fixture/theme, extending component-explorer startup and CI duration.
Findings.Evidence: This call precedes options.render at fixtureUtils.ts:1207. registerFixtureSyntaxHighlighting awaits acquire; FixtureTextMateTokenizerInstance.create builds Oniguruma/TMGrammarFactory and seven language grammars, while TMGrammarFactory invokes the XHR-backed readFixtureTextResource for loaded scopes. FixtureTextMateTokenizers clears its instance when the fixture-owned final reference is disposed. baseUI.fixture.ts demonstrates many fixtures with no text models.
Findings.Recommendation: Gate setup behind an editor/syntax-highlighting fixture capability enabled only for fixtures that create highlighted models, or retain one run-scoped installation across serial fixture renders rather than owning the final reference in each fixture store.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or capture a non-editor component fixture such as Base UI Buttons/Toggles in explorer or screenshot/CI mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: actualRender must complete setupTheme, ensure the canonical dark theme is loaded, and await registerFixtureSyntaxHighlighting before options.render can create the component. TextMate setup is therefore directly on first paint/capture's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold load per browser-page lifetime because onigLibPromise remains cached; shared across overlapping and later serial fixtures after success.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Oniguruma resource was loaded on the generic fixture render path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first fixture cannot invoke options.render until WASM loading and loadWASM finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read TextMate grammar resources through XMLHttpRequest and parse them in vscode-textmate
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Seven root languages are requested concurrently; their needed descriptor/injection scopes come from an eleven-file descriptor set. One shared set serves overlapping fixtures, but serial last-reference disposal permits another set for each following fixture/theme.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Generic fixtures did not read or parse TextMate grammar resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All requested grammar creation promises must settle before the component render callback runs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of fixture/theme renders. Base UI alone defines eight screenshot fixtures, normally with Dark and Light variants, and repository-wide fixture definitions are numerous; none of these Base UI fixtures creates a text model.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Seven root-language grammar creations are launched with Promise.all. Concurrent overlapping fixtures coalesce through one _instancePromise and share one instance; serial fixtures do not overlap, and fixture disposal drops the final reference and clears the instance.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The dark theme load is cached by WeakMap and Oniguruma initialization is cached by onigLibPromise. Grammar/tokenizer instances are cached only while at least one fixture reference is active; after final disposal, later serial fixtures recreate the grammar factory and parse grammars. Browser caching may make resource bytes warm but does not remove XHR completion, parsing, or tokenizer construction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added await, acquisition chain, resource loader, Promise.all grammar construction, and final-reference teardown are all explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact milliseconds depend on native versus HTTP serving, browser cache warmth, and how much fixture overlap the host schedules. The unconditional reachability and repeated serial construction are not uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: non-editor fixtures gain heavyweight initialization unrelated to their output, and common serial capture can repeat grammar construction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render editor and multi-diff fixtures that create highlighted text models
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The same TextMate setup completes before options.render. Each createTextModel then synchronously force-tokenizes through the model's final line before the fixture render promise can settle and capture can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load and parse the shared TextMate runtime and grammar resources
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialization per overlapping fixture group, potentially repeated after serial final-reference disposal; shared by all models in that group.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editor fixtures created models without the TextMate runtime/grammar resource boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Models are not created until initialization completes because options.render runs afterward.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total lines across models created by one fixture. Existing call sites create roughly one to six models; inspected multi-diff inputs are bounded samples, including 20-line unchanged blocks and short source snippets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Grammar initialization uses the coalesced shared promise and concurrent root grammar creation. forceTokenization itself runs synchronously per model in call order, with no limiter or worker boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tokenizer supports are shared while fixture references overlap. Each model stores its own tokens; forcing to the last line avoids later work for those lines but performs all line tokenization eagerly.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for O(total model lines) synchronous CPU work; moderate for material impact because present fixture inputs are small and deterministic highlighting before capture is intentional.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future fixtures could provide larger models, but current inspected model samples and model counts are modest. No measured evidence establishes a separate user-visible regression from force-tokenizing these bounded screenshot fixtures.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: synchronous full-model tokenization is newly eager but currently bounded by small fixture models and directly serves deterministic highlighted screenshots. The unconditional setup affecting non-editor fixtures is covered by the reported finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render multiple fixtures concurrently in explorer UI and dispose them independently
Scenarios.CriticalPath: All overlapping renders await the same _instancePromise; once initialized, each creates only host-scoped token CSS before its own options.render. Disposal decrements the shared reference count.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously mounted fixtures and token color-map entries used to generate one style element per fixture host.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initialization is correctly coalesced by _instancePromise. The reference count retains tokenizers until the final active fixture disposes; no duplicate grammar burst occurs among overlapping acquisitions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm overlapping acquisitions reuse the same tokenizer instance and Oniguruma promise. Each fixture generates its own scoped CSS; final disposal releases tokenizer supports and permits recreation for a later non-overlapping group.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for coalescing and lifecycle behavior based on the implementation and explicit fixtureUtils comment that explorer UI renders fixtures in parallel.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The explorer's typical overlap count and color-map size affect CSS generation cost, but no evidence shows material rendering or allocation impact from one scoped style per mounted fixture.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: concurrent initialization is coalesced and cleanup is reference-counted; the remaining concern is unnecessary critical-path initialization for fixtures without models.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and traced fixture render startup, tokenizer acquisition/disposal, grammar resource loading, model creation, and synchronous tokenization. Reported one unconditional eager TextMate initialization regression. No concrete regression-fix signal was present.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
